title: Money
summary: The currency is the dong, VND. Cards work in cities. Cash still pays for markets, countryside meals, and many tickets. The number of zeros is the thing that causes mistakes.

sections.heading: Cash and cards
paragraphs: ATMs are common in cities and tourist towns. Tell your bank you are traveling. Withdraw larger amounts less often, and check the fee screen before you confirm.
A 50,000 note and a 500,000 note are easy to confuse when you are tired. Count the zeros before you hand a note over, and count the change.

sections.heading: How people pay
paragraphs: Hotels, malls, and many restaurants in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City take cards. Street stalls, markets, homestays, and boat tickets often want cash. USD is sometimes quoted at hotels; you can almost always pay in dong.

faqs.a: A small backup is useful. Do not plan to pay daily expenses in USD.

seoTitle: Money in Vietnam — dong, ATMs, and cards
seoDescription: How to pay in Vietnam, why cash still matters, and how to read the zeros on a dong note.
